title: Critical: double-booking fix on same-day returns
summary: AutoComplete cron compared dropoff_date < NOW() at date-only granularity. MySQL cast YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00, so any confirmed booking with a same-day dropoff was auto-completed at midnight — long before the actual return time. has_overlap() then skipped these wrongly-completed bookings (status filter excluded 'completed'), allowing the same vehicle to be double-booked for the remaining rental hours. Three-layer fix: cron switched to datetime-based selection (end_ts UNIX primary + date+time fallback), has_overlap gains a defense-in-depth status filter for completed+future-end bookings, Status transition matrix allows completed → in_progress for cleanup. Maintenance script included.
changes: Fix (critical): AutoComplete cron now uses _mhm_end_ts (UNIX) as primary, CONCAT(dropoff_date, dropoff_time) fallback (defaults to 23:59:59 if dropoff_time missing — never auto-completes mid-day). Legacy _mhm_end_date fallback preserved.

Fix: has_overlap() defense-in-depth — 'completed' bookings whose end_ts is still in the future continue to block availability (handles future manual status mishaps and was the immediate fix for the cron bug).

changes: Security hardening — Phase B (client side): client-side counterpart of the 3-layer server-side defense against Pro-feature source-edit bypass. Pairs with mhm-license-server v1.9.0+. Layer 1 — every successful activate/validate response is HMAC-verified with MHM_RENTIVA_LICENSE_RESPONSE_HMAC_SECRET; tampered responses no longer unlock Pro and surface a tampered_response error. Layer 2 — new public REST route /wp-json/mhm-rentiva-verify/v1/ping HMAC-answers the server's X-MHM-Challenge header during activation, proving the site is reachable and shares the ping secret. Layer 3 — Mode::canUseVendorMarketplace(), canUseMessages(), canUseAdvancedReports(), and canUseVendorPayout() no longer trust LicenseManager::isActive() alone; they read the feature flag from the server's HMAC-signed feature token (24h TTL). changes: Fix (architectural): The v4.27.1 and v4.27.2 data cleanup migrations never executed on upgraded sites — only on fresh installs. The `plugins_loaded` migration trigger bailed out of ALL migrations whenever the stored plugin version matched the file constant, but `mhm_rentiva_single_site_activation()` stamps that version BEFORE the next `plugins_loaded` fires. After a ZIP-replace upgrade the drift check short-circuited and the new cleanups were skipped forever — this is why mhmrentiva.com still showed Brand Name = '1' and Currency = '1' after upgrading from v4.27.0. Fix: migration trigger now runs on two independent lanes. Lane A (schema drift via DatabaseMigrator) stays version-gated. Lane B (per-flag data cleanups — migrate_remove_auto_populated_labels, migrate_clean_test_pollution) runs on every admin request; each migration returns early once its own flag is set. Three new regression tests in tests/Migration/MigrationLaneIndependenceTest.php prove both migrations execute when the version stamp is already current.

WP's common.js relocator uses jQuery .before() which clones the notice for every matched marker except the last, producing a ghost duplicate.
